questions.question: What do you need to transport hazardous materials?
questions.correctAnswerText: Get a hazardous materials endorsement.
questions.explanation: You must have a hazardous materials endorsement to transport hazardous materials that require placards on your vehicle.

questions.question: Why is hanging meat cargo usually a problem?

options.text: It is dangerous because of its smell.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is unstable.
questions.explanation: Hanging meat is unstable because it has a high center of gravity. The swinging meat can also affect how you control the vehicle.

questions.question: What should you ensure about your truck's load?

options.text: Most cargo is in the front of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: The truck is properly loaded.
questions.explanation: Proper loading is essential for safe operation. Bad loading can hurt how the truck handles, damage the vehicle, and cause cargo to fall and hurt people.

questions.question: How does an empty truck stop compared to a full truck?

options.text: It stops in a shorter distance.
It stops in a longer distance.
It takes the same distance to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: It stops in a longer distance.
questions.explanation: Empty trucks need more distance to stop because they have less weight. This means less traction on the road.

questions.question: What is a problem with retarders?

options.text: They may not be allowed everywhere.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may not be allowed everywhere.
questions.explanation: Retarders help slow a vehicle and reduce brake use. However, they can be loud and some areas do not allow them.

questions.question: How do you check automatic transmission fluid in some vehicles?
questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the engine running.
questions.explanation: In some vehicles, you must keep the engine running when checking the automatic transmission fluid level.

questions.question: What should you look for when checking power steering hoses?
questions.correctAnswerText: Leaks.
questions.explanation: During a pre-trip inspection, check power steering hoses, pumps, and fluid level. Look especially for leaks in the hoses.

questions.question: What should you do if a vehicle is tailgating you?
questions.correctAnswerText: Let the vehicle pass.
questions.explanation: If someone is following too closely, create more space in front of your vehicle so they can pass safely. Speeding up will not help because they may just tailgate you at the higher speed, making it more dangerous.

questions.question: What happens if the exhaust system does not work properly?

options.text: Poisonous fumes may enter the cab.
Fumes may exit from the rear muffler.
You may not be able to steer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Poisonous fumes may enter the cab.
questions.explanation: Exhaust system leaks are very dangerous. They can allow toxic fumes into the cab or sleeper berth, harming drivers and passengers.

questions.question: How can you avoid becoming an aggressive driver?

options.text: Assume other drivers have good reasons for their actions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume other drivers have good reasons for their actions.
questions.explanation: To avoid aggressive driving, give other drivers the benefit of the doubt. Assume they have valid reasons for what they do and do not take their actions personally.

questions.question: When driving, it is important that you:

options.text: Think ahead about how to avoid dangerous situations.
Turn your head all the way around instead of using mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Think ahead about how to avoid dangerous situations.
questions.explanation: While driving, watch the road for hazards. Plan what you will do if a hazard becomes an emergency.

questions.question: A commercial motor vehicle should:

options.text: Not have a fire extinguisher unless it carries hazardous materials.
Not have a fire extinguisher unless it travels through remote areas.
Have a fire extinguisher and other emergency equipment.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have a fire extinguisher and other emergency equipment.
questions.explanation: All commercial motor vehicles must have emergency equipment. This includes spare fuses, three red reflective triangles or flares, and at least one fire extinguisher that is charged and rated properly.

questions.question: A vehicle that is smaller than your vehicle:

options.text: Can usually stop faster than your vehicle.
Usually takes longer to stop than your vehicle.
Takes about the same time to stop as your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can usually stop faster than your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Smaller vehicles generally stop faster than larger vehicles. Remember this when deciding how far back to follow other vehicles.

questions.question: Broken suspension parts:

options.text: Should be repaired, but not right away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must be repaired right away.
questions.explanation: The suspension system holds up the vehicle and keeps the axles in place. Broken suspension parts are very dangerous and must be fixed immediately.

questions.question: Bridges usually:
questions.correctAnswerText: Freeze before other road surfaces.
questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before the rest of the road. Be extra careful on bridges when the temperature is near freezing.

questions.question: The tire load is stated:

options.text: On the side of the tire.
On the inside of the tire.
On the inside of the driver's door.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the side of the tire.
questions.explanation: The tire load is the maximum safe weight a tire can carry at a given pressure. This information is printed on the side of each tire.

questions.question: If another driver is tailgating you, you should:

options.text: Increase the distance between you and the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the distance between you and the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, move farther away from the vehicle in front of you. This gives you more space to stop smoothly and gives the tailgater room to pass. Do not speed up, as this can make the situation more dangerous.

questions.question: To avoid a hazard:

options.text: You may be able to drive onto the shoulder.
You should steer sharply in one direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be able to drive onto the shoulder.
questions.explanation: In an emergency, driving onto the shoulder may be the best way to avoid a hazard. Most shoulders are strong enough to support large vehicles.

questions.question: If a five-foot-long item is placed on a flatbed trailer, it must be secured by at least:
questions.correctAnswerText: Two tie-downs.
questions.explanation: Cargo needs one tie-down for every 10 feet of length. However, always use at least two tie-downs, even for small cargo.

questions.question: Which of the following items can never be transported in the passenger compartment of a bus?
questions.correctAnswerText: Radioactive materials
questions.explanation: Buses can never carry labeled radioactive materials where passengers sit. Small arms ammunition labeled ORM-D and emergency hospital supplies are allowed.
